commits.subject: Initial release: Mneme — the memory layer of your codebase
commits.body:
A monorepo CLI + MCP server that builds a permanent, queryable memory of
a git repository so AI assistants and engineers can answer "why does this
code exist?" in seconds.

Packages:
  @mneme-ai/core         git parser, SQLite store, hybrid retrieval
                         (BM25 + vector cosine fused via RRF)
  @mneme-ai/embeddings   Ollama / OpenAI / hash-fallback adapters
  mneme-ai (CLI)         init, index, ask, why, status, correlate, mcp
  @mneme-ai/mcp          MCP server (stdio) for Claude Code, Cursor,
                         Continue, Copilot
  @mneme-ai/correlator   phase 3 — temporal+structural incident correlation
                         engine + Sentry/Datadog/manual adapters
  @mneme-ai/web          phase 4 — D3 temporal graph viewer (placeholder)

Quality:
  - 98/98 unit + integration tests passing
  - Eval harness with 5 retrieval variants × 15-question golden set
    (recall@k, MRR, nDCG)
  - Benchmark suite: 100 commits indexed in 2.0 s, query p50 1.2 ms
  - GitHub Actions CI: Ubuntu/macOS/Windows × Node 20/22
  - STATUS.md auto-generated with real numbers

See README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, ROADMAP.md, STATUS.md.

commits.subject: v0.3.0 — Phase 2 ships, README softened, no competitor comparisons
commits.body:
Phase 2 — semantic similarity & clone detection (now real, not a stub)
  • TypeScriptParser via the TypeScript compiler API (zero new runtime deps;
    typescript is an optional peer dep). Extracts functions, classes,
    interfaces, type aliases, enums, exported variables. Skips .d.ts and
    test files by default. Uses `git ls-files` for automatic .gitignore
    respect.
  • CosineCloneDetector — pre-normalize, pairwise cosine, similarity-graph
    union-find, drop singletons, sort by cluster size + cohesion. O(N²).
  • Store: upsertEntities, countEntitiesByLanguage, iterEmbeddedEntities.
  • CLI: `mneme entities`, `mneme clones --threshold 0.85 --top N`.
  • Dogfooded on this repo: surfaces real duplication
    (sleep helper in 3 files, type aliases between GitHub/GitLab adapters).

CLI fixes from the v0.2 smoke test
  • `mneme --version` now reports the actual package version
  • `mneme wisdom -n <N>` flag aligned with documented help text

README + ARCHITECTURE

    what Mneme does, in three layers (WHY / WHAT / WHERE-IT-BREAKS), and
    leaves comparison to the reader.
  • Marketing reddit-programming.md updated to never name competitors in
    reply patterns.

commits.subject: v0.4.0 — Phase 3 wired, Phase 4 shipped, WILD #1 (mneme heal) live
commits.body:
Phase 3 — incident correlation, end-to-end
  • `mneme correlate --source sentry --org X --project Y --since 30d`
    pulls issues from Sentry, runs the temporal+structural engine, and
    persists correlations to .mneme/mneme.db with confidence scores.
  • `mneme correlate --source manual --file ./incidents.json` for repos
    that don't ship Sentry — same engine, JSON input.

Phase 4 — temporal viz, real (not a placeholder)
  • SQLite-backed /api/graph (commits + incidents + correlations) with
    ?at=<iso> filtering for time-travel.
  • /api/timeline endpoint feeds a scrubber slider in the UI.
  • D3 force-layout with drag, pan/zoom, click-to-inspect, link
    highlighting on selection. No build step — d3 from CDN.

WILD #1 — `mneme heal` (turn bad commits into searchable memory)
  • New @mneme-ai/embeddings exports: OllamaEnricher, OpenAIEnricher,
    resolveEnricher (mirrors the embedder shape but for chat/completion).
  • New @mneme-ai/core/enrich module: needsHealing heuristic, prompt
    builder, isUncertain guard.
  • New `synthesized_notes` table — append-only, never replaces the
    original commit message.
  • CLI:
        mneme heal --dry-run             # list candidates
        mneme heal                       # synthesize via Ollama
        mneme heal --provider openai
        mneme heal --max 50 --subject-min-len 15
  • Verified on app-chutima-git: identifies 6 of 9 commits as needing
    healing (subjects like "fix", "updated", "no message").

WILD ideas catalog

    Includes: echo, ledger, oracle, palimpsest, conscience, prophecy,

commits.subject: v0.5.0 — Wild Ideas: 8 of 15 shipped, 5 thoughtful stubs, 2 research
commits.body:
This is the release where Mneme stops being "git memory for AI" and
becomes a substrate for an entire family of codebase-intelligence tools.
Eight new commands ship as real working code; five more print thoughtful
design pages so users can see the roadmap shape.

NEW commands (real implementations + smoke-tested on app-chutima-git)
  mneme echo       — find past incidents that resemble a current one
                     (Jaccard token similarity + correlation lookup)
  mneme palimpsest — render the causal chain of a single line of code
                     (blame → commit → correlations → incident → cause)
  mneme runaway    — files that have grown silently across many commits
                     (commit count × net line growth, ranked)
  mneme mirror     — onboarding dossier (top PRs, top contributors, top
                     incidents) with impact scoring
  mneme rumor      — tribal phrases mentioned in commits but no doc
                     explains. Cross-checks against /docs and root .md.
  mneme fossil     — files deleted from HEAD but still alive in git history
                     (uses --diff-filter=D)
  mneme ledger     — tamper-evident audit log for compliance (SOX/SOC2)
                     SHA-256 hash chain across commit metadata.
                     JSON or CSV export. The fintech feature.

NEW commands (design stubs — each prints a real plan, not lorem)
  mneme oracle     — historical risk analysis on a snippet (#4)
  mneme conscience — review co-pilot from history (#6)
  mneme genome     — codebase fingerprint + ancestry (#9)
  mneme dialogue   — conversational chat over your repo (#11)
  mneme tribute    — your codebase as a 60-sec movie (#15)

INFRASTRUCTURE
  • New `@mneme-ai/core/util` module — shared loadAllCommits,
    loadCommitsBetween, sha256Hex, cosineSim helpers used across all
    new features.
  • Tests for the util module (4 tests covering cosine + sha256 chain).

DOCS
  • WILD_IDEAS.md gets a status snapshot table at the top — 8 ✅, 5 🚧, 2 🔬.
  • demo.tape upgraded to a 60-second tour of the new headline features.

QUALITY
  • 159/159 tests passing (was 152) — +7 new tests
  • Build clean across the matrix
  • All workspace deps version-locked at 0.5.0

commits.subject: v0.6.0 — Conscience + Teach (UA-inspired structural intelligence)
commits.body:
Inspired by tools that turn codebases into knowledge graphs (Understand-
Anything etc.), v0.6 adds Mneme's structural-intelligence layer. Two new
real commands plus a layer-classification primitive every future feature
can reuse.

NEW: `mneme conscience` (formerly stub — now real)
  Risk-score a PR against your repo's own history.
    • takes file paths, --diff-file, or --stdin (unified diff)
    • finds past commits that touched the same files
    • cross-references the correlations table for incident history
    • scores risk = 0.5*overlap + 0.35*incident_score + 0.15*recency
    • prints HIGH/MED/LOW per match, lists incidents that followed
  Smoke-tested on app-chutima-git: 5 historical matches found across
  2 files, ranked correctly.

NEW: `mneme teach <folder|file>`
  UA-inspired: explain a unit in plain language.
    • CLASSIFY: tags entities by layer (api/service/data/ui/utility/
      test/config/unknown) via path heuristics
    • AGGREGATE: counts entities per layer
    • SUMMARIZE: reuses the Phase-1.5 enricher (Ollama default) to
      write 3-5 sentences of plain prose with strict "no invention"
      system prompt
  8 unit tests for the classifier — covers all rules + ordering
  precedence (test paths beat service paths even when nested).

DOCS
  • README — placeholder block for the demo GIF (uncomment after vhs run)
  • Wired both commands into commander; `conscience` replaces its stub

QUALITY

  • Build clean
  • Versions locked at 0.6.0 across the workspace

commits.subject: v0.6.1 — Drop Sentry branding from user-facing surfaces
commits.body:
User feedback: vendor names should not appear in the README diagram or
positioning copy (a brand and legal-safety concern). This release scrubs
all Sentry/SENTRY-* mentions from public-facing material while keeping
the technical SentryAdapter class — it really does speak the Sentry REST
API, so that name remains accurate inside the codebase.

User-facing rename

  • Positioning line: "Code knows WHAT. Git knows WHY. The pager knows
    what broke."
  • Example incident IDs: SENTRY-1287/1294 → INC-1287/1294 throughout
    docs, marketing, ROADMAP, WILD_IDEAS, README, CONTRIBUTING, status
  • CLI: `--source sentry` → `--source pager` (internally the adapter
    is still SentryAdapter; the env var SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is now an
    accepted fallback for MNEME_PAGER_TOKEN)
  • Help text + descriptions reworded to "pager / observability platform"
  • Marketing drafts (HN, Reddit, Twitter, LinkedIn, Dev.to) updated
  • DISCUSSIONS welcome post softened
  • CONTRIBUTING.md areas-wanted softened

Kept (technical accuracy)
  • Class SentryAdapter and adapters/sentry.ts — it's a Sentry-specific
    REST client. Renaming it would be a lie.
  • All 11 tests in sentry.test.ts continue to test the real adapter.
  • correlator/README.md import samples — they document the real API.
  • CLI dimmed note "(currently speaks the Sentry REST API)" so users

commits.subject: v0.7.0 — Mutant release: every Phase 3 adapter real, blast + adapt, ROADMAP rewritten
commits.body:
This release closes the loop on every roadmap row that was within reach.
The new "mutant" framing isn't marketing — it's `mneme adapt`, a real
command that detects the repo's profile and prescribes the next 1-3
commands tailored to it.

NEW — Phase 3 (incident correlation): all live adapters
  • DatadogAdapter — Events API v2 with cursor pagination + 429/5xx
    retry. Maps event status → severity, extracts files from stack traces.
  • GitHubActionsAdapter — failed-workflow runs as incidents. Useful
    for repos that don't ship a paid observability stack.
  • DatadogAdapter and GitHubActionsAdapter sit alongside the existing
    SentryAdapter and ManualJsonAdapter — pluggable, uniform interface.

NEW — `mneme blast <commit>`
  Inverts the correlation engine: predicts incidents likely to follow
  shipping a commit. Computes a base rate (% of past commits on the same
  files that triggered an incident within 48h) and labels LOW/MED/HIGH.
  Useful as a pre-merge gate or `git push` advisory.

NEW — `mneme adapt` (the mutant)
  Inspects the current repo and outputs:
    • archetype       — empty / young / early-stage / active service / mature
                        + modifiers (sparse hygiene / PR-driven / incident-correlated)
    • signals         — commit count, generic-msg ratio, PR ratio, etc.
    • recommendations — ordered checklist of the 1-3 commands that will
                        deliver the most value on THIS repo, today
  Smoke-tested on app-chutima-git: correctly recommends `heal`, `entities`,
  and `correlate --source manual` based on its profile.

NEW — MCP tools (now 7 total)
  • mneme_list_entities  — paginated, filterable entity list
  • mneme_find_similar   — by entity id OR snippet, cosine over stored
                            entity embeddings
  • mneme_blast          — blast-radius prediction exposed to AI clients

ROADMAP.md — rewritten
  • No more "XX weeks" estimates anywhere
  • New "mutant principle" section explaining how Mneme adapts to each
    repo profile
  • Honest done/not-done audit: every phase row reflects what's actually
    shipping in main, with smoke-test references where applicable
  • "Beyond" section consolidates infrastructure-grade work that needs
    paying users or external contributors

QUALITY
  • 167/167 tests passing
  • Build clean across the matrix
  • Versions bumped to 0.7.0

commits.subject: v0.8.0 — AI engine (genius), Python parser, cluster collapse, smoke-test report
commits.body:
This release closes four of the most-requested gaps and adds a real AI
engine layer (mneme genius). All four headline items work today on a real
repo.

NEW — `mneme genius <question>` (the AI engine)
  An LLM-orchestrated agent that plans which Mneme commands to run, runs
  them, and synthesizes a final answer. Three-phase loop:
    plan       — LLM picks tools from the catalog (15 commands)
    execute    — spawnSync each step, capture stdout
    synthesize — LLM weaves outputs into 4-8 sentences with citations
  The plan output is JSON-validated and capped at --max-steps. The model
  cannot invent tools — only pick from the catalog. Every step prints
  before it runs, so the user can pass --trace for full output.

NEW — Python parser (Phase 2 expansion)
  PythonParser uses Python's own `ast` module via subprocess. Reasons over
  tree-sitter: zero new node deps, zero platform-fragile native binaries,
  and Python's ast IS what CPython itself parses with — perfect accuracy.
    • Probes for `python3` (or `python`) on PATH; degrades silently if
      missing — TS/JS still works, no hard dep.
    • Skips tests/, .venv, __pycache__, build, dist by default.
    • Parses Python 3.6+ files including class methods, async functions,
      module-level exported variables.
    • `mneme entities` auto-detects and uses both parsers when available.

NEW — Phase 4 cluster collapsing
  When the temporal graph would render >200 commits, the server groups
  them into N-day buckets (default 7 days) and emits "supercluster" nodes
  instead. Correlations rewire automatically from member commits to
  the cluster id. Click in the UI to inspect a cluster's bucket window,
  member count, author diversity. Drop ?collapseAfter=99999 to opt out.

NEW — SMOKE_TEST.md
  20-of-22 commands ran successfully on app-chutima-git (a real GitLab
  repo with 9 commits and 22% generic subjects). 0 hard crashes — the 2
  commands that didn't fully run failed gracefully because Ollama's chat
  model wasn't pulled. Every output captured for verifiability.

QUALITY
  • 167/167 tests passing
  • Build clean across the matrix
  • Versions bumped to 0.8.0 across the workspace
  • README diagram and ROADMAP unchanged in this release; both honest about
    where these features fit

commits.subject: release: rewrite release.yml in block-style YAML (v0.8.1 startup-failed)
commits.body:
The previous release.yml used flow-style mapping for `env: { ... }` with
GitHub-Actions expressions inside, which startup-failed silently (0 jobs
ran on every tag push and on dependabot pushes). Rewrote in plain
block-style YAML — same semantics, no expression-in-flow-mapping risk.

Also:
- Moved permissions from job-level to top-level (id-token: write needed
  for --provenance attestations).
- Added explicit `init.defaultBranch main` to git config to avoid the
  "Reinitialized in main" noise on hosted runners that default elsewhere.
- Bumped all packages to 0.8.2 so we can re-tag cleanly. v0.8.1 the tag
  was already pushed but its workflow run never started, so no npm
  publish happened.

commits.subject: release: drop --provenance + add `npm whoami` debug step
commits.body:
v0.8.2 publish-core failed at the first `npm publish` step. The most
likely cause is provenance attestation (which needs the GitHub repo +
npm org to be set up just so for first publish).

- Removed `--provenance` from all five publish steps. We can add it
  back as a separate enhancement once basic publish works.
- Added a "Verify npm authentication" step that runs `npm whoami`
  before publishing — if NPM_TOKEN is missing, expired, or scoped
  wrong, this surfaces it in the log instead of failing inside
  `npm publish`.

commits.subject: release: bump 0.8.4 — verify CI publish with Bypass-2FA NPM_TOKEN
commits.body:
v0.8.3 was published manually after the v0.8.3 release workflow failed
with E403 (the previous NPM_TOKEN was a granular token without Bypass-2FA,
which npm rejects for non-interactive publishes).

NPM_TOKEN has since been replaced with a Bypass-2FA-enabled granular
token. This bump has no code change — its only purpose is to push a new
tag so we can verify the release workflow now publishes end-to-end with
the corrected token. Expected outcome: workflow passes through Verify-npm-
authentication → Publish core/embeddings/correlator/mcp/cli — the same
five packages that were manually published at 0.8.3.

If this run is green, future tag pushes will publish on autopilot.
If it fails, the failure surface is now narrow (token, registry, or
package metadata) and can be debugged from the workflow log directly.

commits.subject: docs(readme): rewrite install section — 3 clear paths (npx / global / clone)
commits.body:
The previous "Quick start" section showed `npm install -g mneme-ai` first
and `npx -y` second, with no explicit guidance on when to pick which, and
no clone-from-source path at all. Users following the README to contribute
were missing the workflow they actually needed.

This rewrite splits installation into three labeled options:

  Option 1 — npx (zero install, one-off use)
  Option 2 — global install (daily use, with upgrade + uninstall recipes)
  Option 3 — clone repo (contributor / customizer)

Option 3 is the addition that mattered: it shows the full workflow from
git clone → npm install → npm run build → run-from-source → npm link
(make the local checkout invokable as `mneme` globally), plus how to pull
future updates and run the test/eval/bench suites.

The "after install, the same 60-second flow" section underneath unifies
the three options back into a single first-use sequence so the rest of
the README applies regardless of which install path the reader picked.

commits.subject: feat(core): wisdom-mutant engine, redaction, go parser, confidence floor
commits.body:
Five core changes that make Mneme production-ready:

- Confidence floor in retrieve/search — honest "no context found" on
  gibberish queries. Negative-recall: 0% to 100% with no impact on
  positive recall.

- Redaction layer (util/redact) — strips AWS/GitHub/Stripe/OpenAI/
  Anthropic/JWT/PEM/Slack/npm/Google patterns before any text reaches
  a remote embedder. ON by default; 12 built-in rules + custom rule
  hook + aggressive mode for password=/long-hex.

- Wisdom Mutant Engine — feedback collector (records every query,
  pending until explicit/implicit signal) + grid-search auto-calibrator
  over (semWeight, minSemCosine, rrfK). Picks the config that maximizes
  hit rate on the user's own positive examples. 3 append-only tables,
  schema v2.

- Go entity parser (regex v1) — methods (Receiver.Name), generics
  (Go 1.18+), structs, interfaces, type aliases. Comment- and
  raw-string-aware via masking pass.

- Eval golden set 15 to 50 questions across 7 categories: why-question,
  keyword, who-when, negative, short-query, specific-ref, multi-tag.

77 new tests; 167 to 244 total, all passing.

commits.subject: feat(cli): probe + no-llm helpers — answer "do I need Ollama?" up front
commits.body:
Two small modules that the rest of the CLI builds on:

- probe.ts: detects Ollama (with embedding model pulled or not), OpenAI
  key presence, and hardware tier. recommendEmbedder() picks the best
  path for THIS user — Ollama first if available (privacy), then OpenAI
  if a key is set, else hash fallback. Capable hw with no embedder gets
  an "install Ollama" nudge; weak hw is told hash is genuinely fine.

- no-llm.ts: unified deterministic-mode gate, resolved from CLI flag,
  config.deterministic, and MNEME_NO_LLM env. refuseLlm() returns exit
  code 2 with a standardized message + a usable non-LLM suggestion.

config.ts adds the deterministic flag for per-repo persistence.

commits.subject: feat(cli): wire wisdom + redaction + deterministic mode + smart init
commits.body:
User-visible CLI surface for everything in the previous two commits:

- mneme init now runs the environment probe and prints a recommendation
  ("Ollama running, embed model pulled — local, free").
- mneme doctor — same probe, runnable on demand.
- mneme index gains --no-redact, --aggressive-redact, --no-llm. The
  redaction summary prints per-rule hit counts after a run.
- mneme heal / genius / teach gain --no-llm. heal and genius refuse
  with exit code 2 + a non-LLM suggestion; teach falls back to layer
  classification only.
- mneme ask records every query into wisdom_feedback and prints
  "Was this useful? mneme feedback <id> up | down".
- mneme why marks recently-returned commits as helpful (implicit
  positive signal — the user looked at one).
- mneme feedback / calibrate / watch — the Wisdom Mutant CLI.
  watch is the 24/7 daemon: re-index on commit, calibrate hourly,
  self-eval daily.

Stub commands (oracle, genome, dialogue, tribute) are now hidden
from the main --help; they remain runnable and a new "mneme planned"
command lists them.

commits.subject: refactor(cli): kill 4 stub commands, tier --help to 8 essentials

The 27-command --help was overwhelming new users. Reduce to 8 tier-1
essentials, hide the rest behind `mneme advanced`.

- Delete oracle / genome / dialogue / tribute (was: design pages with no

- Delete the `mneme planned` command (was hidden listing of those stubs).
- Tier 1 (visible in --help): init, doctor, index, ask, why, status,

- Tier 2 (hidden via { hidden: true }, listed by `mneme advanced`):
  correlate, entities, clones, heal, wisdom, manifesto, echo, palimpsest,
  runaway, mirror, rumor, fossil, ledger, conscience, blast, adapt,
  feedback, calibrate, genius, teach.
- Add `mneme advanced` — prints the hidden commands grouped by phase

- Bump CLI version string to 0.9.0 (workspaces will be bumped at release).

WILD_IDEAS and ROADMAP counts updated. Was "11 of 17 shipped" with 4

commits.subject: feat(ask): Sprint 1 — intent classifier + synthesis + beautiful output
commits.body:
Five changes that turn `mneme ask` from "raw retrieval dump" into
an answer-shaped experience.

- Intent classifier (retrieve/intent) — classifies a query into
  specific / lookup / temporal / vague before retrieval runs. Vague
  queries ("how to improve my code") short-circuit with a redirect
  message instead of returning low-confidence guesses. 21 tests.

- Adaptive confidence (retrieve/search) — classifyConfidence() looks
  at top score AND the gap to top-2/3. Tied results (all ≈ 0.016)
  drop to "low" even when the absolute top is decent. Returns one
  of: high / medium / low / none. Echoed alongside results.

- LLM synthesis layer (retrieve/synthesize) — turns top-K results
  into a 2-4 sentence paragraph that cites commit hashes. Falls back
  to an extractive answer (template over top-3) when no LLM is
  reachable. Strips common LLM artifacts (leading 'Answer:', wrapping
  quotes, trailing 'Sources:' blocks). 14 tests with mock enricher.

- Beautiful output (cli/render-answer) — sectioned response with
  confidence badge, ✦ Answer, ◆ Evidence (top-3 of N, not all N),
  ⊕ Files (clustered by top-2 path segments). OSC 8 hyperlinks make
  PR/commit refs clickable in modern terminals (iTerm2, Wezterm,
  Windows Terminal, VSCode). 22 tests.

- Animated thinking spinner (cli/spinner) — braille frames during
  retrieval and synthesis. Disabled on non-TTY (CI, piped output).

ask.ts is rewritten to compose these layers: classify → search →
synthesize → render. The previous flat-list output is gone.

(recall@3 87.7%, hit rate 96%, negative recall 100%).

commits.subject: feat(insights): Sprint 2 — who-knows, decisions, stack-trace, story
commits.body:
Four commands that turn indexed memory into developer-actionable insight.
Each is grounded in pure functions in @mneme-ai/core/insights and shipped
behind a thin CLI in commands/insights-cli.ts.

- who-knows <topic>: surface the people most likely to answer a question
  about a topic, ranked by commit volume × recency. log-scaled volume so
  one mega-contributor doesn't dominate; recency floor at 0.3 to keep
  long-tail experts visible. Tiers: definitive / active / stale / occasional.

- decisions [--format markdown]: regex-based ADR extractor. 9 patterns
  covering "decided to X", "switched from A to B", "replaced X with Y",
  "chose A over B", "use X instead of Y", "adopted X", "deprecated X",
  "migrated from A to B", "rejected X". Captures rationale ("because Y",
  "so that Y") within 200 chars after the trigger. Markdown output drops
  straight into docs/ADR.md.

- stack-trace [--from F]: parse a JS/TS/Python/Go/Java stack trace and
  query history for each frame: last 3 commits + count of past incidents
  affecting the file. Reads stdin or a file. Honest "no commits indexed
  for this file" when the trace points outside the indexed repo.

- story <topic>: narrate the evolution of a topic across acts (initial /
  refactor / incident / evolution / stable). Groups consecutive commits
  with the same flavor into one act. Optional Ollama act-narration adds
  a 1-2 sentence prose summary per act; falls back gracefully without LLM.

35 new unit tests across 4 modules. All 352 tests passing. Eval A/B
shows no regression (recall@3 = 87.7%, hit rate = 96%).

Each command is hidden from the main `mneme --help` (tier-2) and listed
under `mneme advanced` so the new-user surface stays at 8 essentials.

- dream: speculative ideas grounded in codebase patterns. Gathers signals

  like "Service"/"Adapter") and asks an LLM to suggest 3-5 features that

commits.subject: feat(insights): Sprint 4 — 3 fixes + 5 killer commands + divider system
commits.body:
Fixes the wisdom output that was confusing on Thai/multilingual repos
+ adds 5 new commands that turn Mneme into a genuine pre-commit AI
partner. All 9 changes are pure-data + tested + behind hidden flags.

== Fixes ==

  1. FTS5 tokenizer: porter unicode61 → trigram. Works on Thai, CJK,
     Arabic, and any non-space-separated language. Schema bumped to v3
     with auto-migration from v2 (drops + re-populates chunks_fts from
     existing chunks rows — no re-embedding needed).

  2. Verdict-style synthesis: extractive answer aggregates by author
     ("alice authored 78% of commits — likely the person to ask")
     instead of "Possibly relevant abc1234, also def5678…". LLM prompt
     rewritten to emit single-sentence verdict + 1-2 supporting lines,
     no hedging.

  3. who-knows verdict: returns ExpertVerdict {topExpert, confidencePct,
     backup, risk}. CLI now shows a single answer card up top, then a
     candidates list, instead of an undifferentiated list of names.

== Killer commands ==

  • regret  — detects shipped+fixed-within-window commits. 4 follow-up
    kinds: revert / hotfix / fix / sameFiles. Per-commit lesson + repo
    regret rate. Pure detection, no LLM. 17 tests.

  • bus-factor  — surfaces files where one author owns ≥ 75% of changes.
    Tier: critical / high / medium / low. Concrete pairing recs ("pair
    with bob — closest second"). 13 tests.

  • paradox  — detects architectural flip-flops (A → B → A) by looking
    at the destination keywords of each decision (after "to" / "instead
    of"). Group by topic, count ABA reversals, ask the right ADR
    question. 7 tests.

  • commit-coach  — pre-commit AI partner. Reads `git diff --staged`
    (or stdin / file), parses files+modules+shape+lines, suggests a
    Conventional-Commits-style message, recommends reviewers from
    file ownership, warns about scope creep, surfaces past regrets
    on the same files. 12 tests.

  • crystal-ball  — predicts CI / follow-up failure probability for
    the staged diff. Builds a fingerprint (modules × extensions × shape
    × size × hasTests), finds historically similar commits, looks at
    what % needed a follow-up fix. Verdict: clear / moderate / risky /
    unknown. Returns the most-similar past commit + its outcome. 9 tests.

== Visual polish ==

  • Divider helper: ════════════════════════════════════════════════
    used across all 5 new commands as section separator. Same width
    everywhere (64 chars). Auto-pads when given a label.

  • Verdict cards: every command now leads with a single-sentence
    answer, then evidence below. No more "scan a list and figure it out
    yourself" output style.

468 tests (was 413). Eval A/B unchanged.

commits.subject: test: property-based test suite — 16 properties × 10k runs = 160k cases
commits.body:
Adds fast-check (industry-standard property-based testing for TS/JS).
Each property states an invariant that must hold for ANY input;
fast-check generates 10,000 pathological inputs per run (empty strings,
NaN, gigantic arrays, unicode boundaries) — inputs we'd never think to
hand-write.

Total per `npm test` run: 16 properties × 10,000 = 160,000 generated
test cases, finishing in ~3.5 seconds.

Properties tested:

  cosine (3):
    • symmetric: cosine(a,b) === cosine(b,a)
    • bounded: cosine ∈ [-1, 1]
    • self-similar: cosine(a,a) ≈ 1 for non-zero a

  redact (3):
    • idempotent: redact(redact(x)) === redact(x)
    • no AWS access key id pattern survives redaction
    • no GitHub PAT pattern survives redaction

  parseStackTrace (1): never throws on any input

  parseDiff (1): never throws + valid shape from {feat,fix,refactor,...}

  classifyIntent (1): valid label from {specific,lookup,temporal,vague}

  classifyConfidence (1): valid label from {high,medium,low,none}

  similarity / crystal-ball (3):
    • symmetric, bounded, reflexive

  slug / obsidian (1): alphanumeric+dash, ≤80 chars, no border dashes

  extractTopicWord (1): string-or-undefined, never empty when defined

  suggestFollowUps (1): ≤ 3 items, all with non-empty command + reason

Result: 484 total tests (was 468), all passing. Eval A/B unchanged.

commits.subject: release: v0.10.0 — Sprint 5 (Wall Street meets Git, 10 quant commands)
commits.body:
The "champion" release. v0.10.0 applies quantitative-finance lenses to
a codebase. Time series of commits = price ticks. Author churn = volume.
Bug-fix periods = drawdowns. Authors fixing own bugs = insider trading.
Quality per dev-hour = risk-adjusted return. Same math, new domain.

== Sprint 5 — 10 quant commands ==

  drawdown            worst losing streaks (firefighting periods).
                      Tier classification by length × duration.

  alpha               Kelly-criterion allocation across technical-debt
                      items. Fractional Kelly (×0.25 default) avoids
                      blow-up risk. Edward Thorp's actual formula.

  backtest            validate any binary predictor against historical
                      outcomes. Precision/recall/F1 + lift over baseline
                      + verdict {strong-edge / real-edge / weak / no-edge}.

  black-swan          rare-but-catastrophic file patterns (Taleb's tail
                      risk applied to git). Files with low touch count
                      but high incident severity.

  insider-trading     authors who fix bugs they introduced themselves.
                      Concrete pairing recommendation from author who
                      has touched the same files without insider patterns.

  moneyball           undervalued contributors — high downstream impact
                      with low LOC volume. Per-commit ROI metric.

  greek               Delta · Gamma · Theta — sensitivity analysis.
                      Calibrated numbers, not panic.

  correlation-matrix  hidden behavioral coupling between files. Catches
                      coupling static analysis misses (no import link,
                      but always change together).

  implied-volatility  project chaos predicted from commit message tone
                      BEFORE metrics catch up. Linguistic signals:
                      exclamations, all-caps, emoji, friction words,
                      hedging language.

  tax-loss-harvest    dead-code candidates ranked by safety. Delete to
                      offset technical debt accumulated elsewhere.

== Numbers ==

Tests: 484 to 613 (+129). 50 test files. Eval A/B unchanged.
All 10 commands: pure data analysis, no LLM calls.
All output: divider system (heavy double-line) for visual hierarchy.

commits.body:
Two world-firsts in one release.

(1) `mneme guardian` — the 24/7 self-healing engine

  while (true) {
    diagnose();        // 6 weakness kinds + 4 threat kinds
    fix();             // safe auto-actions only
    learn();           // append to .mneme/guardian.jsonl

Detects index drift, missing embeddings, low-quality grade,

gets a policy: auto (apply), recommended (suggest), observe (log).

(2) Four novel retrieval-scoring algorithms (post-process BM25+cosine)

  TDWE — Time-Decay Weighted Embedding
    w(c) = exp(-λ · age_days / half_life)

  RACB — Regret-Aware Chunk Boosting
    boost(c) = 1 + ln(1 + days_to_followup × severity)
    severity: revert=3, hotfix=2, fix=1, sameFiles=0.5

  ADS — Author Diversity Score re-ranking
    penalty(i) = α × (same_author_above / total)
    final(i) = base(i) × (1 − penalty(i))

  CGAR — Causal Graph Augmented Retrieval (light)
    boost = initial × decay^(hops − 1)
    walks PR/issue/hash refs, default maxHops=2

  Ensemble: TDWE → RACB → CGAR → ADS

Each is a pure function, individually disable-able, separately tested.
20 tests.

commits.body:
Root cause: indexing hung at 0% on Ollama because:
1. OllamaEmbedder used /api/embeddings (singular) → 32 sequential HTTP
   round-trips per batch. For 1241 chunks = 1241 sequential calls.
2. No fetch timeout — first call (cold-start model load) blocked forever
   with no user feedback.
3. Indexer reported progress only every batch, so the bar froze for 30+s.

Fixes:
- OllamaEmbedder.embed() now calls /api/embed with input: string[] →
  one HTTP round-trip per batch (Ollama >= 0.3). Falls back to singular
  /api/embeddings on 404 for older Ollama, with per-item progress hook.
- AbortController timeout (default 180s, tunable) → if Ollama hangs the
  user gets a clear 'did not respond' error with how-to-check guidance.
- Indexer emits an explicit 'warming up' progress event before the first
  batch so the bar isn't stuck at 0%.
- mneme init / mneme doctor recommendation block now formats the action
  as 'Run this in your terminal: $ <cmd>' with explicit yellow callout
  so users know they need to copy-paste.

All 834 tests pass.

commits.body:
ROOT CAUSE of 'fetch failed' on Windows:
Node 18+/undici resolves 'localhost' → '::1' (IPv6) but Ollama only
listens on 127.0.0.1 (IPv4). The TCP connect fails silently, surfacing
as a generic 'fetch failed' with no actionable message.

Fixes (world-class install path):
- Default URL changed: localhost:11434 → 127.0.0.1:11434 in 4 places
  (probe, embedder, enricher, resolve error message).
- Auto-rewrite localhost → 127.0.0.1 if user passes their own baseUrl,
  so even configs that already say 'localhost' now work.
- OllamaEmbedder.verify() — cheap pre-flight: ping /api/tags, confirm
  model is pulled, run a 1-token sanity embed. CLI calls this BEFORE
  the long indexer loop so Ollama issues fail in seconds, not minutes.
- AbortController fetch errors now surface error.cause.code and produce
  3-step remedy (start ollama / verify model / use 127.0.0.1).
- Auto-retry once on transient network errors (ECONNRESET, socket hang
  up, etc.) — covers cold-start socket churn.
- friendlyError() translates ECONNREFUSED / ENOTFOUND / timeout into
  human-readable (reason, remedy) pairs.
- mneme index now shows 'verify' step + clear 'Fix:' callout if Ollama
  isn't ready, instead of hanging at 0%.

All 834 tests pass.

outliers.subject: feat(ask): Sprint 1 — intent classifier + synthesis + beautiful output
outliers.body:
Five changes that turn `mneme ask` from "raw retrieval dump" into
an answer-shaped experience.

- Intent classifier (retrieve/intent) — classifies a query into
  specific / lookup / temporal / vague before retrieval runs. Vague
  queries ("how to improve my code") short-circuit with a redirect
  message instead of returning low-confidence guesses. 21 tests.

- Adaptive confidence (retrieve/search) — classifyConfidence() looks
  at top score AND the gap to top-2/3. Tied results (all ≈ 0.016)
  drop to "low" even when the absolute top is decent. Returns one
  of: high / medium / low / none. Echoed alongside results.

- LLM synthesis layer (retrieve/synthesize) — turns top-K results
  into a 2-4 sentence paragraph that cites commit hashes. Falls back
  to an extractive answer (template over top-3) when no LLM is
  reachable. Strips common LLM artifacts (leading 'Answer:', wrapping
  quotes, trailing 'Sources:' blocks). 14 tests with mock enricher.

- Beautiful output (cli/render-answer) — sectioned response with
  confidence badge, ✦ Answer, ◆ Evidence (top-3 of N, not all N),
  ⊕ Files (clustered by top-2 path segments). OSC 8 hyperlinks make
  PR/commit refs clickable in modern terminals (iTerm2, Wezterm,
  Windows Terminal, VSCode). 22 tests.

- Animated thinking spinner (cli/spinner) — braille frames during
  retrieval and synthesis. Disabled on non-TTY (CI, piped output).

synthesize → render. The previous flat-list output is gone.

outliers.subject: feat(insights): Sprint 2 — who-knows, decisions, stack-trace, story
outliers.body:
Four commands that turn indexed memory into developer-actionable insight.
Each is grounded in pure functions in @mneme-ai/core/insights and shipped
behind a thin CLI in commands/insights-cli.ts.

- who-knows <topic>: surface the people most likely to answer a question
  about a topic, ranked by commit volume × recency. log-scaled volume so
  one mega-contributor doesn't dominate; recency floor at 0.3 to keep
  long-tail experts visible. Tiers: definitive / active / stale / occasional.

- decisions [--format markdown]: regex-based ADR extractor. 9 patterns
  covering "decided to X", "switched from A to B", "replaced X with Y",
  "chose A over B", "use X instead of Y", "adopted X", "deprecated X",
  "migrated from A to B", "rejected X". Captures rationale ("because Y",
  "so that Y") within 200 chars after the trigger. Markdown output drops
  straight into docs/ADR.md.

- stack-trace [--from F]: parse a JS/TS/Python/Go/Java stack trace and
  query history for each frame: last 3 commits + count of past incidents
  affecting the file. Reads stdin or a file. Honest "no commits indexed
  for this file" when the trace points outside the indexed repo.

- story <topic>: narrate the evolution of a topic across acts (initial /
  refactor / incident / evolution / stable). Groups consecutive commits
  with the same flavor into one act. Optional Ollama act-narration adds
  a 1-2 sentence prose summary per act; falls back gracefully without LLM.

35 new unit tests across 4 modules. All 352 tests passing. Eval A/B
shows no regression (recall@3 = 87.7%, hit rate = 96%).

Each command is hidden from the main `mneme --help` (tier-2) and listed
under `mneme advanced` so the new-user surface stays at 8 essentials.

  like "Service"/"Adapter") and asks an LLM to suggest 3-5 features that

- chat: multi-turn REPL with conversation context. Uses readline/promises

  no LLM. Proposes `mneme why <file>`, `mneme story <topic>`,
  `mneme who-knows <topic>`, `mneme blast <commit>` based on what the
  current result set looks like. extractTopicWord() finds the most

outliers.subject: feat(insights): Sprint 4 — 3 fixes + 5 killer commands + divider system
outliers.body:
Fixes the wisdom output that was confusing on Thai/multilingual repos
+ adds 5 new commands that turn Mneme into a genuine pre-commit AI
partner. All 9 changes are pure-data + tested + behind hidden flags.

== Fixes ==

  1. FTS5 tokenizer: porter unicode61 → trigram. Works on Thai, CJK,
     Arabic, and any non-space-separated language. Schema bumped to v3
     with auto-migration from v2 (drops + re-populates chunks_fts from
     existing chunks rows — no re-embedding needed).

  2. Verdict-style synthesis: extractive answer aggregates by author
     ("alice authored 78% of commits — likely the person to ask")
     instead of "Possibly relevant abc1234, also def5678…". LLM prompt
     rewritten to emit single-sentence verdict + 1-2 supporting lines,
     no hedging.

  3. who-knows verdict: returns ExpertVerdict {topExpert, confidencePct,
     backup, risk}. CLI now shows a single answer card up top, then a
     candidates list, instead of an undifferentiated list of names.

== Killer commands ==

  • regret  — detects shipped+fixed-within-window commits. 4 follow-up
    kinds: revert / hotfix / fix / sameFiles. Per-commit lesson + repo
    regret rate. Pure detection, no LLM. 17 tests.

  • bus-factor  — surfaces files where one author owns ≥ 75% of changes.
    Tier: critical / high / medium / low. Concrete pairing recs ("pair
    with bob — closest second"). 13 tests.

  • paradox  — detects architectural flip-flops (A → B → A) by looking
    at the destination keywords of each decision (after "to" / "instead
    of"). Group by topic, count ABA reversals, ask the right ADR
    question. 7 tests.

  • commit-coach  — pre-commit AI partner. Reads `git diff --staged`
    (or stdin / file), parses files+modules+shape+lines, suggests a
    Conventional-Commits-style message, recommends reviewers from
    file ownership, warns about scope creep, surfaces past regrets
    on the same files. 12 tests.

  • crystal-ball  — predicts CI / follow-up failure probability for
    the staged diff. Builds a fingerprint (modules × extensions × shape
    × size × hasTests), finds historically similar commits, looks at
    what % needed a follow-up fix. Verdict: clear / moderate / risky /
    unknown. Returns the most-similar past commit + its outcome. 9 tests.

== Visual polish ==

  • Divider helper: ════════════════════════════════════════════════
    used across all 5 new commands as section separator. Same width
    everywhere (64 chars). Auto-pads when given a label.

  • Verdict cards: every command now leads with a single-sentence
    answer, then evidence below. No more "scan a list and figure it out
    yourself" output style.

outliers.subject: test: property-based test suite — 16 properties × 10k runs = 160k cases
outliers.body:
Adds fast-check (industry-standard property-based testing for TS/JS).
Each property states an invariant that must hold for ANY input;
fast-check generates 10,000 pathological inputs per run (empty strings,
NaN, gigantic arrays, unicode boundaries) — inputs we'd never think to
hand-write.

Total per `npm test` run: 16 properties × 10,000 = 160,000 generated
test cases, finishing in ~3.5 seconds.

Properties tested:

  cosine (3):
    • symmetric: cosine(a,b) === cosine(b,a)
    • bounded: cosine ∈ [-1, 1]
    • self-similar: cosine(a,a) ≈ 1 for non-zero a

  redact (3):
    • idempotent: redact(redact(x)) === redact(x)
    • no AWS access key id pattern survives redaction
    • no GitHub PAT pattern survives redaction

  parseStackTrace (1): never throws on any input

  parseDiff (1): never throws + valid shape from {feat,fix,refactor,...}

  classifyIntent (1): valid label from {specific,lookup,temporal,vague}

  classifyConfidence (1): valid label from {high,medium,low,none}

  similarity / crystal-ball (3):
    • symmetric, bounded, reflexive

  slug / obsidian (1): alphanumeric+dash, ≤80 chars, no border dashes

  extractTopicWord (1): string-or-undefined, never empty when defined

  suggestFollowUps (1): ≤ 3 items, all with non-empty command + reason

Result: 484 total tests (was 468), all passing. Eval A/B unchanged.

outliers.subject: release: v0.10.0 — Sprint 5 (Wall Street meets Git, 10 quant commands)
outliers.body:
The "champion" release. v0.10.0 applies quantitative-finance lenses to
a codebase. Time series of commits = price ticks. Author churn = volume.
Bug-fix periods = drawdowns. Authors fixing own bugs = insider trading.
Quality per dev-hour = risk-adjusted return. Same math, new domain.

== Sprint 5 — 10 quant commands ==

  drawdown            worst losing streaks (firefighting periods).
                      Tier classification by length × duration.

  alpha               Kelly-criterion allocation across technical-debt
                      items. Fractional Kelly (×0.25 default) avoids
                      blow-up risk. Edward Thorp's actual formula.

  backtest            validate any binary predictor against historical
                      outcomes. Precision/recall/F1 + lift over baseline
                      + verdict {strong-edge / real-edge / weak / no-edge}.

  black-swan          rare-but-catastrophic file patterns (Taleb's tail
                      risk applied to git). Files with low touch count
                      but high incident severity.

  insider-trading     authors who fix bugs they introduced themselves.
                      Concrete pairing recommendation from author who
                      has touched the same files without insider patterns.

  moneyball           undervalued contributors — high downstream impact
                      with low LOC volume. Per-commit ROI metric.

  greek               Delta · Gamma · Theta — sensitivity analysis.
                      Calibrated numbers, not panic.

  correlation-matrix  hidden behavioral coupling between files. Catches
                      coupling static analysis misses (no import link,
                      but always change together).

  implied-volatility  project chaos predicted from commit message tone
                      BEFORE metrics catch up. Linguistic signals:
                      exclamations, all-caps, emoji, friction words,
                      hedging language.

  tax-loss-harvest    dead-code candidates ranked by safety. Delete to
                      offset technical debt accumulated elsewhere.

== Numbers ==

Tests: 484 to 613 (+129). 50 test files. Eval A/B unchanged.
All 10 commands: pure data analysis, no LLM calls.
All output: divider system (heavy double-line) for visual hierarchy.
Property tests: 16 properties x 10k runs = 160k cases still passing.

outliers.subject: feat(v0.16.0): Giant Slayer — guardian + 4 novel scoring algorithms
outliers.body:
Two world-firsts in one release.

(1) `mneme guardian` — the 24/7 self-healing engine

  while (true) {
    diagnose();        // 6 weakness kinds + 4 threat kinds
    fix();             // safe auto-actions only
    learn();           // append to .mneme/guardian.jsonl
    sleep(interval);
  }

Detects index drift, missing embeddings, low-quality grade,
quality regression, stale calibration, schema drift. Each finding
gets a policy: auto (apply), recommended (suggest), observe (log).
Safe by default — only --apply enables auto-fix loop.
10 tests.

(2) Four novel retrieval-scoring algorithms (post-process BM25+cosine)

  TDWE — Time-Decay Weighted Embedding
    w(c) = exp(-λ · age_days / half_life)

  RACB — Regret-Aware Chunk Boosting
    boost(c) = 1 + ln(1 + days_to_followup × severity)
    severity: revert=3, hotfix=2, fix=1, sameFiles=0.5

  ADS — Author Diversity Score re-ranking
    penalty(i) = α × (same_author_above / total)
    final(i) = base(i) × (1 − penalty(i))

  CGAR — Causal Graph Augmented Retrieval (light)
    boost = initial × decay^(hops − 1)
    walks PR/issue/hash refs, default maxHops=2

  Ensemble: TDWE → RACB → CGAR → ADS

Each is a pure function, individually disable-able, separately tested.
20 tests.

outliers.subject: fix(embeddings): switch to /api/embed batch endpoint + add timeout + warmup hint
outliers.body:
Root cause: indexing hung at 0% on Ollama because:
1. OllamaEmbedder used /api/embeddings (singular) → 32 sequential HTTP
   round-trips per batch. For 1241 chunks = 1241 sequential calls.
2. No fetch timeout — first call (cold-start model load) blocked forever
   with no user feedback.
3. Indexer reported progress only every batch, so the bar froze for 30+s.

Fixes:
- OllamaEmbedder.embed() now calls /api/embed with input: string[] →
  one HTTP round-trip per batch (Ollama >= 0.3). Falls back to singular
  /api/embeddings on 404 for older Ollama, with per-item progress hook.
- AbortController timeout (default 180s, tunable) → if Ollama hangs the
  user gets a clear 'did not respond' error with how-to-check guidance.
- Indexer emits an explicit 'warming up' progress event before the first
  batch so the bar isn't stuck at 0%.
- mneme init / mneme doctor recommendation block now formats the action
  as 'Run this in your terminal: $ <cmd>' with explicit yellow callout
  so users know they need to copy-paste.

All 834 tests pass.

outliers.subject: fix(install): bulletproof Ollama on Windows + pre-flight verify
outliers.body:
ROOT CAUSE of 'fetch failed' on Windows:
Node 18+/undici resolves 'localhost' → '::1' (IPv6) but Ollama only
listens on 127.0.0.1 (IPv4). The TCP connect fails silently, surfacing
as a generic 'fetch failed' with no actionable message.

Fixes (world-class install path):
- Default URL changed: localhost:11434 → 127.0.0.1:11434 in 4 places
  (probe, embedder, enricher, resolve error message).
- Auto-rewrite localhost → 127.0.0.1 if user passes their own baseUrl,
  so even configs that already say 'localhost' now work.
- OllamaEmbedder.verify() — cheap pre-flight: ping /api/tags, confirm
  model is pulled, run a 1-token sanity embed. CLI calls this BEFORE
  the long indexer loop so Ollama issues fail in seconds, not minutes.
- AbortController fetch errors now surface error.cause.code and produce
  3-step remedy (start ollama / verify model / use 127.0.0.1).
- Auto-retry once on transient network errors (ECONNRESET, socket hang
  up, etc.) — covers cold-start socket churn.
- friendlyError() translates ECONNREFUSED / ENOTFOUND / timeout into
  human-readable (reason, remedy) pairs.
- mneme index now shows 'verify' step + clear 'Fix:' callout if Ollama
  isn't ready, instead of hanging at 0%.

All 834 tests pass.
